pages.name: Government
pages.html:
Government

Each value below has its own heading. Links from generated worlds open this page at the value.

Step 5: Government; Roll 2D-7 and add the population code to determine the average governing system found on the world.

0: None

No formal governing structure except for family and interpersonal relationships.

  • Tech Level DM (p.94): +1

1: Company/Corporation

For-profit organizations run by managerial elites who govern the citizenry with corporate organizational structures. Corpo-feudal, private-sponsored colonies, etc.

2: Participating Democracy

The citizens have a direct voice in the ruling functions of government via direct democratic methods and assemblies.

3: Self-Perpetuating Oligarchy

The government is led by an elite class who maintains power with minimal to no input from the general population.

4: Representative Democracy

Laws and government are dictated by elected individuals from the general population.

5: Feudal Technocracy

Government functions within a caste-based structure driven by technological implementation.

  • Tech Level DM (p.94): +1

6: Captive Government

Imposed leader or puppet government controlled by an outside government, to govern the local population.

7: Balkanisation

No central government. Decentralized, small political governments in perpetual conflict and rivalries driven by philosophical, ecological, economical, and social factors. Laws are determined by the local government.

  • Tech Level DM (p.94): +2

8: Civil Service Bureaucracy

The governing duties are driven by government agencies led by groups and individuals with specific expertise from the general population to maintain civil function and services for everyone.

9: Impersonal Bureaucracy

Governing responsibilities are driven by agencies without input or from the population. Leaders are insulated from the effects of government stagnation.

A: Charismatic Dictator

A single leader determines the rule of law and the direction of society, functioning as a representation of the people they govern, prioritising their culture and influence over others.

B: Non-Charismatic Leader

An impersonal leader who determines the government without popular enthusiasm.

C: Charismatic Oligarchy

The population elevates an elite few to drive society in an ideal direction. The chosen few have the full confidence of the many.

D: Religious Sovereignty

A religious organisation determines the roles of government, driven by spiritual determinants in law and society.

  • Tech Level DM (p.94): -2

E: Religious Autocracy

A single individual or small group has absolute power over the many via “divine right” and religious authority.

  • Tech Level DM (p.94): -2

F: Totalitarian Oligarchy

Government is used to force the will of the few onto the many, often with oppressive and coercive methods to maintain and exercise power, to limit the rights of most of the population.

The chart on p.90 calls government D Religious Dictatorship; the table on p.92 calls it Religious Sovereignty. We use p.92.

Book p.92

pages.name: Travel Zones
pages.html:
Travel Zones

Each value below has its own heading. Links from generated worlds open this page at the value.

Step 10: Zone Types: Determine if the main world has a Amber or Red Zone.

Green

No Amber or Red Zone: the world has no zone code. (The book does not name this case; Green is this system's label.)

A: Amber Zone

  • Amber Zone: Amber Zones are places where travelling to is discouraged due to environmental, political, or social reasons that could be dangerous.
  • Amber Zones are designated for the following worlds: Atmosphere 10+ and Government Codes 0, 7, or 10 with Law Level 0 or 9+.

R: Red Zone

  • Red Zone: Red Zones are banned areas that are either overtly dangerous locations or are sanctuary planets intending to preserve the local ecology, culture, or environment from outside interference. Travelling into Red Zone planets is considered extremely risky, either for personal safety or legally.
  • Red Zones are designated for any planet with an ongoing war, which has a prominent criminal faction that is in control, or is a Low Tech world (5 or less) without a starport.

Book p.95
